title: Immutable data-plane swap orchestrator with traffic-ceding and rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Background: Private (VPC) customers require guaranteed continuity during data-plane/runtime upgrades. Current in-place rolling upgrades have exposed transient errors during cache rehydration and tail-latency spikes for stateful tenants. Goal: implement an immutable-swap orchestrator that performs a host-level data-plane exchange (blue->green style) driven by IaC/Terraform and the runtime operator, with first-class traffic ceding, priming, health gating, and an automated rollback playbook. The implementation must work for hosted private deployments and on-prem bundles and be configurable per-tenant (slice) via the deployment manifest.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrades can be executed without >1% overall error-rate increase across active tenants
SLOs (p95 latency, availability) are preserved within configured guardrails during canaries
Automatic rollback triggers when any safety metric breaches thresholds for more than 2 minutes
Rollout can be aborted and fully reverted within 10 minutes to previous data-plane image
Terraform module exposes a single declarative toggle to start an immutable swap and an optional dry-run
Audit log entries recorded for each orchestration step and surfaced to the console
design_decisions: Immutable swap vs in-place patching: chosen immutable swap to simplify state transfer and rollback determinism
Traffic ceding implemented at edge proxy layer (Envoy) using weighted routing and active draining hooks
Priming step: background KV cache prewarm using captured traffic replays and synthetic probes before flip
Health gating: quorum of synthetic probes + real traffic SLOs (p95, 5xx rate, cache-hit) must pass to advance
Rollback: automated full-swap to previous image plus cache invalidation fencing; also provide manual quick-revert endpoint
rollout_steps: 1) Plan via Terraform module (dry-run) to create parallel immutable data-plane group
2) Operator brings up new group in isolated VPC slice, runs node-level unit checks
3) Priming: run cache prewarm jobs (replay recent prefixes + synthetic priming probes)
4) Canary: shift 5% traffic via Envoy weight to new group for 10 minutes with enhanced tracing
5) Evaluate: automated checks (latency p95, errors, cache-hit, tail latency) and human review gate
6) Ramp: increase traffic in steps (5 -> 25 -> 60 -> 100) with configurable hold windows
7) Post-swap verification: run end-to-end smoke tests, runbook checklist and mark release complete
8) Cleanup: decommission old group after retention window and produce artifact (upgrade report)
rollback_playbook: Trigger: automated when any of the following breaches for >2m: p95 increases by 25% vs baseline, 5xx rate >0.5% absolute, kv cache hit drops >30%
1) Operator issues: set Terraform state "rollback=true" for the slice
2) Traffic: Envoy weight immediately shifts 100% back to previous group with drain window (30s) and circuit-breaker enforced
3) Validation: run health checks and ensure metrics return to baseline within 5 minutes
4) Postmortem: collect logs, traces, and priming artifacts; tag upgrade run as failed and create incident ticket template
5) Fix forward guidance: if rollback occurs twice for the same image within 24h, block image and notify release manager
test_plan: Unit tests for Terraform module inputs and outputs (plan diff assertions)
Operator e2e with k3s dev cluster to validate lifecycle hooks
Load test: staged canary with k6 script reproducing customer QPS distribution
Chaos test: simulate node termination and slow priming to validate rollback triggers
Integration: Grafana dashboard smoke and trace correlation verification
On-prem acceptance: install bundle test with air-gapped priming scenarios
